title: Make athena audit read landed jobs' files or refuse before paying
summary: The auditor picks the candidate commit if it exists, else the squash commit on main carrying `Athena-Job: <id>`, else none. If the job changed files and none can be read, it errors naming the job and the commits tried before any model call, and writes no record. Audience: maintainers running `athena audit` on landed jobs in fresh clones.

defaults_applied.how: Two new tests plus a unit test for the commit-exists helper; clippy and fmt clean.
Tests assert outcome/ file contents and zero fake driver invocations, not just wiring.
The fix resolves the commit explicitly and fails loudly instead of treating a missing commit as a missing path.
Only auditor.rs, one helper in athena-git, tests and the changelog change.
Error message and changelog entry are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The squash commit is found with the existing Git::log_grep on HEAD (the base branch) for the trailer `Athena-Job: <id>`; a new `commit_exists` helper in athena-git checks `<oid>^{commit}` via rev_parse/cat-file.
Resolution happens in auditor::run before the workspace is created or agent_spec/invoke is called, so a refusal costs nothing and commits no records.
A job whose candidate has no changed files (after filtering records/ and non-plain paths) is still audited as today; only 'changed files exist but nothing readable' is refused.
Deleted files read as Ok(None) from show_file; the refusal fires only if none of the changed files could be read, not if some were deleted while others read.
New tests go in crates/athena-cli/tests/auditor.rs using its existing fixture and fake driver.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: in a test repository where the candidate commit is absent but a squash commit with the `Athena-Job: <id>` trailer exists, the auditor's outcome/ folder holds the changed files' contents from the squash commit (asserted on file content) and exactly one audit is recorded.

Run `cargo test`: with neither commit present, `athena audit <job>` fails with a message naming the job and the commits tried, the fake driver records zero invocations, and no audit or invocation record is written.
Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: existing auditor tests pass unchanged and all are clean.
athena-git gains a small helper telling whether a commit exists; Git::show_file's behavior for a missing path is unchanged.
auditor.rs resolves the commit (candidate, then the trailer-matched commit on the base, then none) and refuses before any model call when the job changed files and none can be read.
CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] states that audits of jobs whose candidate commit is missing read nothing, and what changed; bullets have no blank lines between them.

out_of_scope: The auditor's prompt and what it judges
How candidate commits are stored or fetched
departures: Slightly higher cost than reference: needs new test fixtures (squash commit with trailer, missing candidate) across two crates.
